title: Fake Microsoft Scanner Secretly Sends Victim Banking and Remote Access Data to Telegram
content_md: A new refund scam is using fake Microsoft-branded security scan websites to trick users into removing antivirus software and sharing sensitive information. The sites, which use names such as SysScan, claim to check whether antivirus software is working correctly. Instead, they display alarming but fabricated warnings and tell visitors that their installed antivirus is causing serious problems. The pages falsely claim that Windows no longer supports third-party antivirus products and urge users to uninstall them immediately. This is untrue. Microsoft continues to support third-party antivirus software on Windows. Researchers identified 11 scam sites hosted on the same server. While the domains use different names, they follow the same pattern: show a fake scan, report severe device problems, collect victim data, and prepare users for a fraudulent refund call. Fake Scanner Telegram Heist The scam pages collect browser-accessible data such as operating system details, screen resolution, device memory, processor count, permissions, network information, and browser capabilities. This helps the scan appear legitimate and tailored to the victim’s device. However, the sites cannot inspect a computer for malware, firmware settings, antivirus status, kernel security features , missing Windows patches, or hardware vulnerabilities. Fake Scanner Telegram Heist (Source: malwarebytes) Despite this limitation, the pages display claims that a browser sandbox is compromised, memory is exposed
exclude_reason: Generic refund scam using fake Microsoft branding. Well-documented scam pattern, not a novel vulnerability or significant campaign.
